seoTitle: How to Turn Off Grammarly on Google Docs (2026)
metaDescription: Disable Grammarly in Google Docs for a single document, pause it globally through your browser extensions, or turn it back on when you need it again.
intro: Grammarly's real-time suggestions are helpful, but sometimes you just want an uninterrupted writing session. This guide covers three levels of turning it off: pausing it on the current document only, disabling the browser extension globally, and managing desktop application toggles if you use Grammarly outside the browser too.

steps.heading: Locate the floating widget
steps.body: Find the Grammarly icon positioned inside your active document canvas to access its quick settings.

steps.heading: Pause it for the current document
steps.body: Use the widget's pop-up toggle to stop suggestions specifically on the document you're currently working in.

steps.heading: Open your browser extensions
steps.body: Go to your browser's extensions toolbar to manage Grammarly's background configuration more broadly.

steps.heading: Disable the extension globally
steps.body: Toggle the Grammarly extension off entirely, or restrict its access to specific web domains if you only want it disabled on certain sites.

steps.heading: Check the desktop application
steps.body: If you use the standalone Grammarly desktop app, open its settings to pause system-wide typing suggestions separately.

steps.heading: Re-enable when ready
steps.body: Reverse any of the above toggles once you want real-time editing suggestions back before your final proofreading pass.

faq.question: Can I turn off Grammarly for just one document?
faq.answer: Yes, the floating widget's pop-up toggle lets you pause suggestions specifically for the document you're currently working in.

faq.question: Does disabling the extension delete my Grammarly account?
faq.answer: No, disabling or uninstalling the extension only stops it from running; your account and settings remain intact.

faq.question: Why is Grammarly still active after I closed the widget?
faq.answer: Closing the widget window doesn't always fully disable checking; use the extension toggle in your browser for a complete pause.

faq.question: Do I need to restart my browser after disabling Grammarly?
faq.answer: Usually not, though refreshing the current document tab helps ensure the change takes effect immediately.
